0.headline: How India's IPO boom gave Sebi a revenue windfall
0.heading: How India's IPO boom gave Sebi a revenue windfall
0.intro: India's robust IPO market significantly boosted SEBI's finances as prospectus filing fees surged 27% to Rs 338.3 crore.
0.body:
India's primary market has done more than just enrich founders, private equity investors and investment bankers, instead it has also given the capital markets regulator a sizable boost to its own finances.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) collected Rs 338.3 crore from prospectus filings and offer documents in 2025-26, a sharp 27% increase from Rs 266.3 crore in the previous financial year, according to the regulator's latest annual report.

The jump mirrors another record year for India's IPO market, which saw companies continue to tap public markets despite bouts of volatility, resulting in a steady stream of filing fees flowing to the regulator.

The annual report shows that revenue from "offer documents and prospectus filed" rose to Rs 338.3 crore in 2025-26 from Rs 266.3 crore in 2024-25.

Unlike recurring fees that Sebi collects every year from intermediaries such as stock exchanges, brokers and mutual funds, these are non-recurring charges, making them directly linked to capital-raising activity.

The increase suggests that the wave of IPOs, follow-on public offers and other equity issuances translated into higher regulatory collections.

India has witnessed one of the world's busiest IPO markets over the past two years, with companies across sectors approaching the markets to raise capital or provide exits to existing investors.

During 2025-26, fundraising through equity public issues (IPOs and FPOs) declined by 0.9% compared to 2024-25, reaching Rs 1.9 lakh crore. Despite this dip in value, the number of newly listed companies rose to 366, up from 320 in the previous year.

On the main board, IPOs totalled 109 during the year, with the median issue size increasing to Rs 760 crore from Rs 740 crore in 2024-25. These main board IPOs successfully raised Rs 1.8 lakh crore, marking an 8.9% increase over the previous year.

Overall collections cross Rs 2,500 crore

Overall, Sebi's fee and other charge collections (unaudited) rose to Rs 2,563 crore in 2025-26 from Rs 2,334 crore a year earlier, an increase of nearly 10%. While recurring fees remained the regulator's biggest source of income, several non-recurring streams also saw notable increases.

Among them:

	Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) fees increased to Rs 105 crore from Rs 73.3 crore.
	Mutual fund fees rose to Rs 35.1 crore from Rs 33 crore.
	Fees from stock exchanges climbed to Rs 45.2 crore from Rs 41.1 crore.
	Custodian fees increased to Rs 149.2 crore from Rs 132 crore.

The largest contributor to Sebi's revenue continues to be annual regulatory fees paid by stock exchanges. Recurring fees from stock exchanges increased to Rs 1,349.3 crore in 2025-26 from Rs 1,265.9 crore in the previous year, accounting for more than half of the regulator's total collections.

Fees collected from brokers in the cash market also rose to Rs 61.6 crore from Rs 58.1 crore, reflecting sustained trading activity.

Even as equity markets witnessed periods of correction during the year, companies continued to queue up for listings, ensuring that Sebi benefited alongside the broader ecosystem of exchanges, investment banks and market intermediaries.

With a strong pipeline of companies still awaiting market debuts, the IPO market is likely to remain an important contributor to the regulator's income in the coming year as well.

1.headline: Shiprocket IPO decoded: Smaller issue, bumper exits, key risks and the road ahead
1.heading: Shiprocket IPO decoded: Smaller issue, bumper exits, key risks and the road ahead
1.intro: The logistics-tech company has cut its IPO size by 31 percent, while early backers are looking at returns ranging from 359x to losses at the upper end of the price band.
1.body: Shiprocket is heading to the public markets with a Rs 1,617.48-crore IPO, but with a smaller ask than it had initially planned. The logistics-tech company has cut the issue size by 31% from the Rs 2,342.35 crore proposed in its updated DRHP, trimming both the fresh issue and the investor sell-down. The IPO comprises a Rs 885.5-crore fresh issue and a Rs 731.98-crore offer for sale (OFS). The fresh issue has been reduced from Rs 1,100 crore, while the OFS has been cut from Rs 1,242.35 crore. The price band is set at Rs 92-97 a share. Axis Capital, BofA Securities India, JM Financial and Kotak Mahindra Capital are the book running lead managers to the issue. For Shiprocket, the IPO brings fresh capital to fund its next phase of growth, while allowing some of its earliest backers to cash out. For some investors, the IPO could be a very lucrative payday, while for others, it could mean taking a haircut on their original investment. Founders, early backers eye bumper exits Shiprocket’s IPO is setting up sharply different outcomes for its early backers. At the Rs 97 upper end, some investors are sitting on multi-fold returns, while others are selling below their acquisition cost. Vishesh Khurana stands out, with a WACA of just Rs 0.27. His Rs 20-crore OFS translates to a 359x multiple, or nearly Rs 19.9 crore in gains. Gautam Kapoor and Saahil Goel, with a WACA of Rs 0.28, are each selling shares worth up to Rs 61 crore. That works out to 346x their acquisition cost, or gains of roughly Rs 60.8 crore each. Early investor 500 Startups III is looking at a 77.6x return, while Tribe Capital could make 7.7x, translating to gains of roughly Rs 104 crore on its Rs 120-crore OFS. MCP3 SPV and Agility International could make around 2.1x and 2.6x, respectively. But LR India Fund I and Moore Strategic Ventures are on the other side of the ledger. Their WACAs of Rs 133.94 and Rs 143.82 are above the IPO's upper band, meaning their OFS blocks would fetch only 0.72x and 0.67x their acquisition costs, potential losses of around Rs 103.5 crore and Rs 24.8 crore, respectively. The multiples are calculated by comparing the Rs 97 IPO price with each investor’s disclosed weighted average acquisition cost; gains are based on the maximum OFS value disclosed. Growth gets the biggest slice, debt repayment follows Shiprocket plans to put the bulk of its Rs 885.5-crore fresh issue to work on growth and debt reduction. The company has earmarked Rs 365.6 crore for expanding its platforms, including Rs 205.8 crore for marketing and Rs 159.8 crore for technology infrastructure and capabilities. Another Rs 210 crore will go towards repaying or prepaying borrowings. Together, these account for about 65% of the fresh proceeds. The remaining up to 35% can be used for unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes, leaving room for Shiprocket to pursue inorganic growth. The growth investments will be deployed over FY27-FY29, while the debt repayment is planned entirely for FY27. Losses, vendor dependence cloud the picture Shiprocket’s biggest challenge remains turning growth into sustainable profits. The company says continued investments in its merchant base, products, AI and emerging businesses could keep it under pressure. The business is also heavily dependent on third-party partners. Merchant solution costs accounted for 69.39% of total expenses in FY26, while its top 10 vendors contributed 55.24%. With no exclusive arrangements with logistics partners, Shiprocket is exposed to higher costs, service disruptions and partners prioritising competitors. Competition from marketplaces, aggregators and logistics providers, along with the risks of scaling its nascent cross-border business, add to the pressure. Its legal disclosures show four criminal cases against the company involving Rs 5.39 crore, besides two criminal and seven tax proceedings. Its subsidiaries face another one criminal and three tax proceedings involving Rs 2.34 crore. Separately, a 2022 criminal case names co-founders Saahil Goel and Gautam Kapoor, director Arjun Sethi and CFO Kumar Tanmay, with allegations including cheating, criminal breach of trust, forgery and conspiracy. The case remains pending. Losses narrow sharply, but profits remain elusive Shiprocket remains loss-making despite a sharp improvement in its bottom line over the past two years. Its net loss stood at Rs 79.2 crore in FY26, marginally higher than the Rs 74.4 crore loss in FY25 but sharply lower than the Rs 595.1 crore loss recorded in FY24. The company’s topline continued to grow at a healthy pace, with revenue from operations rising 24% year-on-year to Rs 2,024.1 crore in FY26, following an identical 24% growth in FY25. For Shiprocket, the challenge now is turning that growth into sustainable profitability. The IPO will put that equation under sharper scrutiny as the company uses fresh capital to fund growth, strengthen its technology and expand into newer businesses. The IPO will open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14, with the anchor book opening on August 11.

2.headline: LEAP India IPO subscribed 2% so far on Day 1; GMP at 12%
2.heading: LEAP India IPO subscribed 2% so far on Day 1; GMP at 12%
2.intro: KKR-backed LEAP India's initial public offering (IPO) received a muted response in the early hours of bidding on opening day, with the issue subscribed 2 percent as of 11:00 am on August 7, according to NSE data.
2.body:
KKR-backed LEAP India's initial public offering (IPO) received a muted response in the early hours of bidding on opening day, with the issue subscribed 2 percent as of 11:00 am on August 7, according to NSE data.

The public issue received bids for 26,75,710 shares against 11,49,91,735 shares on offer. The retail investor portion was subscribed 4 percent, while the non-institutional investor (NII) category was booked 2 percent.

The Mumbai-based supply chain management and asset-pooling solutions provider aims to raise Rs 2,480 crore through the public offering, comprising a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 480 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of shares worth Rs 2,000 crore by promoters Vertical Holdings II, backed by KKR, and KIA EBT Scheme 3.

Read Also: Technocraft Ventures IPO subscribed over 15% so far on Day 1; NII segment leads demand, GMP in focus

According to market tracking platform Investorgain, the grey market premium (GMP) for the IPO stood at Rs 18 on August 7, indicating a potential listing gain of 11.5 percent over the upper end of price band.

However, investors should note that the grey market premium is an unofficial market indicator based on speculation and should not be considered a reliable measure of the company's fundamentals or its eventual listing performance.

The IPO, which opened for subscription on August 7, will close on August 11. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 151-159 per share.

Ahead of the issue opening, LEAP India raised Rs 743.62 crore from anchor investors by allotting 4.67 crore equity shares to 32 anchor investors at the upper end of the price band.

The anchor book attracted several marquee global investors, including Smallcap World Fund, the Monetary Authority of Singapore, Morgan Stanley, Norway's Government Pension Fund Global, Cassini Partners, Amundi, Citigroup, Societe Generale and Goldman Sachs.

In addition, six domestic mutual funds inlcuding Axis Mutual Fund, Motilal Oswal AMC, Bank of India Mutual Fund, JM Financial Mutual Fund, ITI Mutual Fund and Groww Mutual Fund participated through 15 schemes. Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance also invested in the anchor round, the company said in its filing.

Before launching the IPO, KKR-backed Vertical Holdings II sold 2.33 crore shares, representing a 5.67 percent stake in LEAP India, for Rs 371 crore through private share purchase agreements. The transaction was separate from the proposed OFS, under which the shareholder plans to sell 12.57 crore shares worth nearly Rs 1,998.6 crore at the upper end of the price band.

Following the transaction, Vertical Holdings II's stake in the company declined to 68.06 percent from 73.73 percent, as disclosed in the red herring prospectus.

Check IPO News Here

Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC's investment vehicle, Gamnat Pte, emerged as the largest buyer in the pre-IPO stake sale after acquiring 1.76 crore shares worth Rs 280 crore, translating into a 4.27 percent pre-issue stake. Other investors included Dymon Asia Multi-Strategy Investment (Singapore), Matyas Possessiones, Insightful Flexicap Fund, Seven Edition Advisory, Gaurav Jaithlia, Krishan Kant Rathi, Pratibha Gupta, Sachin Mahajan and Rowena Ruvet Dsouza.

The company plans to utilise Rs 360 crore from the fresh issue proceeds towards debt repayment, while the remaining funds will be used for general corporate purposes. Proceeds from the OFS will go to the selling shareholders.

JM Financial, Avendus Capital, IIFL Capital Services and UBS Securities India are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

About LEAP India

LEAP India provides technology-enabled supply chain and asset-pooling solutions across industries such as FMCG, food and beverages, third-party logistics, e-commerce, quick commerce, automotive and industrials.
